reviews.reasoning: Span 141.1-141.4 (identity psalm) is a coherent imperative-address unit: the opening vocative “Yahweh, I have called on you” (web:Ps.141.1) through the guard-my-mouth petition (web:Ps.141.3) and the wicked-company petition (web:Ps.141.4) sustain one uninterrupted second-person address; the Hebrew grounding the incense simile at oshb:Ps.141.2 collates at byte tier against the source. Title dual-cite web:Ps.141.0 = oshb:Ps.141.1 is arithmetically correct for this identity psalm (mt_title_verses empty; the title text sits inside MT v1). The row's own rejected_alternative correctly declines an early close at v2, since vv3-4 continue the same address without a topic break; the actual turn to third-person subjects (“the righteous ... him”) at v5 confirms the row's own stated closing boundary. check_refs_mirror, citation_sweep, and the WEB quote check all pass clean on this row.

The span (141.5-141.7) is honestly disclosed as a low-confidence crux, and independent verification supports the row's specific textual observations: v6 (“Their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock”) introduces ‘judges’ with no unambiguous grammatical antecedent in the immediately preceding verses, v7 is rendered as a free-standing quoted image in WEB with no in-verse speaker tag, and no vocative ‘Yahweh’ occurs within vv5-7 while it does occur at v1, v3, and v8 -- all confirmed against the WEB verse text. The medium_low confidence and the device_notes disclosure are appropriate given the genuine textual difficulty of this zone. However, boundary_evidence_refs = [web:Ps.141.4, web:Ps.141.8] does not mirror the specific verses the row argues from in prose: the vv1-5 antecedent-search claim and the vv1,3 vocative claim both reach into web:Ps.141.1-web:Ps.141.3, none of which appear in boundary_evidence_refs.

reviews.reasoning: The whole_psalm unit_type for Ps 142 (7 verses) is policy-correct for a short indivisible psalm, and the rejected_alternative rightly declines a strophe split at v4 since the composition returns to direct first-person address to Yahweh by v5 within too short a psalm to sustain an independent break. The doubled anaphora at oshb:Ps.142.2 collates at byte tier and correctly grounds the opening; the title dual-cite web:Ps.142.0 = oshb:Ps.142.1 is arithmetic-correct for this shift+1 psalm, and the absence of any selah across Ps.142.1-7 is confirmed against both verse_map_web.json and pmarks_Ps.json. Two defects remain. First, Ps 142 is a non-identity (shift+1) psalm, and the row quotes Hebrew content from oshb:Ps.142.2 in both rationale and observed_substrate_signals without ever pairing it to its WEB verse (web:Ps.142.1 = oshb:Ps.142.2) in-field or in boundary_evidence_refs -- the one dual pair present (web:Ps.142.0 = oshb:Ps.142.1) covers only the title, not this content citation, so the non-identity-psalm dual-cite requirement is unmet for the v1/v2 pairing anywhere in the row. Second, observed_substrate_signals embeds a strategy-file section citation in row prose, a register violation independent of the segmentation's own merits.

reviews.reasoning: Span 143.1-143.2 (identity psalm) is a clean two-verse opening: three imperative petitions “Hear ... Listen ... relieve me” (web:Ps.143.1) followed by the legal-metaphor ground “for in your sight no man living is righteous” (web:Ps.143.2), both verbatim-verified. The row correctly identifies that web:Ps.143.3's causal 'For' clause opens a new ground (the enemy's pursuit) rather than continuing the invocation's imperative form, justifying the close at v2. Title dual-cite web:Ps.143.0 = oshb:Ps.143.1 is arithmetic-correct for this identity psalm. confidence=medium is a reasonable, not overclaimed, rating for a short two-verse opening whose boundary rests on a single grammatical shift. No mirror, citation, or quote defects found.

Span 143.3-143.6 tracks the enemy-pursuit and remembering movement through to the selah close; web:Ps.143.6's selah is confirmed present in both verse_map_web.json (web_selah=true) and pmarks_Ps.json (selah at MT 143.6). Since Ps 143 is an identity psalm the in-field dual-cite oshb:Ps.143.6 is arithmetically trivial-but-correct and is, by the book's own scope ruling, an enhancement rather than a requirement here (the MUST applies to non-identity psalms). The quoted spans verbatim-match WEB text, including the ellipsis-joined v3/v5-6 quote. No defect found.

Span 143.7-143.10 is a well-grounded imperative sequence: “Hurry to answer me, Yahweh” (web:Ps.143.7) through the morning plea at oshb:Ps.143.8 and the teach-me petition at oshb:Ps.143.10 (both byte-collated) to “Teach me to do your will” (web:Ps.143.10); independent review of the WEB text confirms all four verses keep unbroken second-person imperative address with no vocative or addressee shift, supporting the span as drawn. One factual claim in observed_substrate_signals is wrong: it states the unit ‘carries no interior disclosure mark’, but pmarks_Ps.json records a paseq mark at every one of the span's four verses (MT 143:7, 143:8, 143:9, 143:10). Paseq is common across this psalm (present at 6 of its 12 verses, including outside the span) and so would not itself have argued for a different boundary, but the absence claim as written is factually incorrect and should not stand as supporting substrate.
